10.1002_adfm.76283: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) have emerged as a promising storage solution, yet their practical application is hindered by severe parasitic reactions in mild acidic electrolytes. In this study, tetrabutylammonium bromide (TBAB) is introduced as a synergistic electrolyte additive to regulate the hydrogen‐bonding environment and ameliorate electrode/electrolyte interfacial chemistry. Combined spectroscopic and computational analyses revealed that TBAB addition could perturb the hydrogen‐bonding network of water molecules and reduce water activity to restrain parasitic reactions, while TBA + adsorption on the zinc surface improved interfacial wettability and homogenized Zn 2+ deposition via electrostatic shielding. This dual mechanism effectively suppressed side reactions and dendrite growth. Zn||Zn symmetric cells with TBAB additive demonstrated prolonged cycling lifespan of over 2400 h at 4 mA cm −2 , 4 mAh cm −2 , an 11‐fold improvement compared to additive‐free cells (220 h). Furthermore, Zn||MnO 2 full cells using 1.0TBAB electrolyte delivered high rate capability and cycling stability, retaining 104 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles (at 0.5 A g −1 ) and 85.5 mAh g −1 after 1000 cycles (at 1.0 A g −1 ). This work highlights the effectiveness of the dual‐functional additive and offers a novel design strategy for engineering aqueous electrolytes for high‐performance AZIBs.
10.1002_aenm.71764: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer‐free catalyst layers based on custom‐made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using as counter‐reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 . The PEMWE cell‐level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst‐coated membrane anode despite lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low‐loading ALD‐made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 . Plasma‐enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower‐activity . Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer‐bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.
10.1039_d6ta02355j: Phosphate buffers selectively dissolve nickel to a depth of approximately 4–6 monolayers on 304 stainless steel anodes, depleting nickel redox-active sites and irreversibly suppressing OER, unlike KOH, which forms a nickel-rich active layer.
